intro: Stand back and take in this portal. You are at the Twin Minaret Madrasa, a madrasa and hospital in Erzurum province, from the late 13th century. It is the largest open-courtyard madrasa in Anatolia. Two brick minarets flank its portal, carved with tree-of-life reliefs at the height of Seljuk stonework.
history: This madrasa was built at the end of the thirteenth century. It is the largest open-courtyard madrasa in Anatolia, and it rises two storeys. Look at the two brick minarets framing the portal, then at the tree-of-life and the double-headed eagle carved on either side of the door: together they are reckoned the summit of Seljuk stonework. And who commissioned it? That is still argued over.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal and the twin brick minarets, then the two-storey courtyard and the Hatuniye tomb.
facts: Did you know? The tomb tower behind the madrasa is the largest Seljuk kümbet in Anatolia, and it shows the building was conceived as a dynastic monument. The madrasa itself is the largest open-courtyard madrasa in Anatolia, and it rises two storeys.
outro: This brings our tour of the Twin Minaret Madrasa to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for your company, and enjoy your visit.
